title: Third-Party & Vendor Coordination Playbook for Enterprise Onboarding
author: Aisha Kapoor
summary: Operational checklist and runbook for coordinating third-party vendors, contractors, and partner integrations during enterprise customer onboarding. Focuses on security/compliance gates, telemetry contracts, cutover orchestration, and escalation paths.
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook documents the recommended coordination model, validation checks, and runbook steps for engaging third-party vendors and external suppliers during an enterprise customer onboarding at Redwood Inference. It covers technical handoffs (SSO, SCIM, KMS), network coupling (VPC peering / firewall rules), telemetry & cost contracts, compliance artifacts, and cross-team escalation flows.

Audience:
- Customer Success Managers (CSMs)
- Solutions Engineers and Onboarding Engineers
- Security & Compliance reviewers
- SRE/Platform contacts
- Third-party vendor leads and integrators

Scope and Assumptions:
- Applies to Dedicated and Private deployments where external parties require access or service integration.
- Assumes an executed contract that approves vendor access scope and data classification.
- Does not replace vendor security questionnaires or legal NDAs; those must be completed pre-engagement.

Key SLA / Acceptance Criteria (customer-facing):
- End-to-end onboarding runway target: 6–8 weeks for standard integrations.
- Security gate acceptance: all required artifacts provided and verified within 10 business days of evidence request.
- Telemetry completeness: 95% of required ingestion metrics flowing into the tenant’s monitoring workspace at canary.
- Post-cutover error rate: <1% p95 error rate for tenant API calls over first 72 hours.

Roles & Responsibilities (quick reference):
- Customer Success (Owner): program management, stakeholder comms, acceptance criteria signoff.
- Onboarding Eng / Solutions Eng: integration templates, test harnesses, runbook execution.
- Security & Compliance: artifact review, risk acceptance, access reviews.
- SRE / Platform: networking (peering, firewall), ingress tuning, throttles.
- Vendor / Third Party: provide integration adapters, required artifacts, point-of-contact for remedial work.

Pre-Onboarding Checklist (must be completed before technical work begins):
1) Contract & Scope
   - Confirm contract includes vendor access, data handling terms, and SLAs.
   - Confirm approved data classification for the integration (PII / Sensitive / Internal).
2) Primary Contacts & RACI
   - Collect primary POC, backup, and escalation contacts (name, role, email, mobile).
   - Share RACI matrix to all parties.
3) Access Requests
   - Vendor must submit an access request ticket in our onboarding tracker with required details: IP ranges, hostnames, SSH keys/public certs, expected egress, and data types.
4) Security Artifacts (deliverables)
   - Vendor SOC2 Type II or equivalent attestation (if applicable).
   - Data processing agreement (DPA) and required clauses executed.
   - Pen test report or summary (last 12 months) or vendor self-attestation.
5) Legal & Procurement signoff documented in the contract binder.

Integration Validation Matrix (examples)
| Integration Type | Minimum Validation Steps | Owner | Pass Criteria |
|------------------|--------------------------|-------|---------------|
| SSO / SAML / OIDC | Exchange metadata, test auth flow, map roles | Onboarding Eng | Successful login, role mapping test users |
| SCIM provisioning | Provision test user, de-provision, attribute mapping | Solutions Eng | Provisioned user appears in tenant, de-provision removes user |
| VPC peering / Firewall | Establish peering, verify routes, egress checks | SRE/Platform | 3x pings, TCP port checks, data path validated via traceroute |
| KMS integration | Key rotation policy, test encrypt/decrypt | Security | Keys accessible with least privilege, decrypt success |
| Event webhooks / Ingest | Replay test events, backpressure handling | Vendor | 99% of events accepted in test window, retry semantics validated |

Detailed Runbook: Cutover Phases (recommended)
1. Preparation Phase (Runway weeks -4 to -1)
   - Week -4: Kickoff meeting with vendor + CSM + Onboarding Eng + Security. Share timelines and acceptance criteria.
   - Week -3: Deliver artifacts (SOC2, DPA, IP ranges). Security begins evidence review and schedules any deep-dive if needed.
   - Week -2: Test environment integration. Establish telemetry streaming (metrics + traces) to the customer’s observability workspace. Validate basic SSO logins and SCIM provisioning for 2 test accounts.
   - Week -1: Dry-run of cutover steps in staging. Run synthetic traffic (at scaled-down level) for 24 hours. Capture telemetry baseline.

2. Canary Cutover (day 0)
   - Start small: route 2–5% of production traffic (or a small tenant slice) to the new integration.
   - Monitor these signals in real-time: 1) request latency p95 < target (customer-specific; default target 300ms), 2) error rate <1% p95, 3) token consumption / cost anomalies < +15% of baseline.
   - Hold for 60–120 minutes of steady state. If thresholds breach, execute rollback procedure (see below).

3. Gradual Ramp (day 0–3)
   - 25% → 50% → 100% increments with 30–60 minute steadiness windows between steps.
   - Re-run provisioning sanity checks and verify no CVE or credential exposure alerts.

4. Post-Cutover Stabilization (day 3–14)
   - Run a focused diagnostics sweep at 24h, 72h, and day 14. Verify: billing signals, latency, error rates, and telemetry coverage.
   - Security to re-run access review and close temporary access granted for cutover.

Rollback Procedure (abbreviated)
1) Immediate trigger conditions:
   - sustained error rate > 2% p95 for 10 consecutive minutes,
   - latency p95 > 2x baseline for 10 consecutive minutes,
   - evidence of data leakage or unauthorized access.
2) Actions:
   1. CSM alerts stakeholders and opens an incident in the tracker.
   2. Onboarding Eng toggles routing to previous integration (or blocks vendor egress IPs) via routing console.
   3. SRE verifies route rollback and runs smoke tests.
   4. Security initiates a focused log and access audit.

Escalation Matrix (primary fast path)
- Level 1 (On-call Onboarding Eng): 30 min response, primary contact Marco Nguyen (eng pager).
- Level 2 (SRE): 60 min response, primary contact SRE rotation (sre-oncall@redwood.ai).
- Level 3 (Security): 2 hour response for evidence review and containment, primary contact Evelyn Park.
- Executive notification: if customer impact > 2 hours or SLA credit likely.

Telemetry & Observability Contract (minimum requirements)
- Metrics: ingest_rate, request_latency_ms.p50/p95/p99, request_error_rate, kv_cache_hit_ratio, token_consumption_per_request.
- Traces: sampled end-to-end traces for 0.1% of requests with correlation_id.
- Logs: structured JSON logs with fields (timestamp, request_id, tenant_id, route, status_code, latency_ms).
- Alerting: on error rate > 1% p95 sustained 5m; on latency p95 > 2x baseline sustained 5m.
- Cost telemetry: daily token consumption and projected 7-day burn rate.

Security & Compliance Gate Checklist (Required Evidence)
- Vendor attestation: SOC2 or equivalent (pdf).
- DPA signed and stored in Contract binder (link to doc repository).
- Network diagram showing peering and ingress/egress flow.
- Access list: issued credentials, service accounts, and scope with TTL and approval stamps.
- Key management proof: KMS integration docs and sample encrypt/decrypt workflow.

Operational Templates (snippets)
- Sample SSH key request text:
  "Please provide the vendor public key (ED25519) for on-call access. Key will be uploaded to the onboarding vault with a 30-day TTL; renewal required after expiration"

- Minimal SCIM provisioning test payload (example):
  {
    "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"],
    "userName": "test.vendor@example.com",
    "name": {"givenName": "Test", "familyName": "Vendor"}
  }

- Telemetry validation curl (example):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <TEST-API-KEY>" https://ingest.redwood-internal.example/tenants/<TENANT>/metrics/status

Acceptance & Post-Go-Live Tasks
- Day 1: Confirm telemetry completeness and backfill any missing events.
- Day 3: Run customer-facing functionality smoke tests and collect signoff from Product/Customer.
- Day 7: Security completes access review; revoke temporary emergency credentials.
- Day 14: CSM prepares QBR inputs: onboarding timeline, integration quality metrics, cost delta, and open action items.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
Q: What if the vendor cannot provide SOC2?
A: We accept equivalent attestations (ISO 27001) or an agreed compensating control plan with a documented timeline and Security risk acceptance.

Q: Who owns the cost delta introduced by vendor traffic?
A: Cost responsibility is contractually defined. During cutover, we enable cost-guardrails and communicate projected overages. CSMs must escalate to finance if projected burn exceeds 15% of baseline.
